What are the conditions for STD testing to be covered by insurance? Explanation of cases and costs for self-pay medical treatment

2024 11/01
PR available
STD test
October 1, 2024November 1, 2024

「I'm worried about a sexually transmitted disease and want to get tested, but is it expensive? ”

「What are the conditions for insurance to apply? ”

Do you have questions like these?

Even if you are worried about a sexually transmitted disease, some people may be unsure about the need for a test because their symptoms are mild, or may be worried that their family members will find out if they take a test.

So in this article,Conditions for insurance coverage for STD tests and treatment methods that will not reveal your identityI will explain about it.

By reading to the end,Acquire correct knowledge about STD testing and eliminate anxiety when undergoing testing.So please refer to it.

Table of contents

STD tests are covered by insurance at the doctor's discretion.

STD tests are covered by insurance based on the doctor's judgment, but only in the following two cases.

Insurance applicable standards
  • If you have symptoms of a sexually transmitted disease
  • If the doctor determines that a sexually transmitted disease test is necessary as a result of the examination

If you are clearly showing symptoms of a sexually transmitted disease, your insurance will cover it.

In addition, even if the symptoms are unclear, if a doctor determines that there is a possibility of a sexually transmitted disease after examination, insurance will be applied, but care must be taken as each hospital has different standards for insurance coverage.

Furthermore,Some clinics perform all STD tests not covered by insurance.Therefore, it is best to check whether your insurance will cover the test before taking the test.

Cases in which STD tests are self-pay medical treatment

We have summarized cases where insurance does not cover the test and you will have to pay the entire test cost yourself.

Cases in which the cost of testing for sexually transmitted diseases must be paid by the individual
  • No symptoms
  • Suffering from a sexually transmitted disease that is difficult to get covered by insurance
  • If you want to take the test anonymously

Let's look at each one one by one.

No symptoms

If you do not have symptoms such as pain or itching, please pay for medical treatment at your own expense.It will be.

Typical sexually transmitted diseases include chlamydia, gonorrhea, genital herpes, and candida.

If you contract these STDs, the following symptoms will mainly appear:

  • pain when urinating
  • genital swelling
  • Pain and itching around the genitals
  • Pus coming out of the genitals
  • There is a strange odor coming from the genitals.
  • A lump or lump appears in the genital area

If you have no symptoms, you run the risk of unknowingly spreading the disease to others, and you may not be aware of the cause of your infertility.

Therefore,Many people get tested because they are worried that they may be infected with a sexually transmitted disease.It is.

However, if you do not have any symptoms, please be aware that insurance will not cover the treatment as it will be treated as a medical examination that is not intended for treatment.

Suffering from a sexually transmitted disease that is difficult to get covered by insurance

There are few cases in Japan.If you have an unfamiliar sexually transmitted disease, it may be difficult to get insurance coverage.Therefore, you may have to pay for the treatment yourself.

For example:

Sexually transmitted diseases that are difficult to get covered by insurance
  • Non-gonococcal, non-chlamydial mycoplasmal urethritis
  • Ureaplasma urethritis

There are a total of four types of bacteria that cause these infections: two types of Mycoplasma and two types of Ureaplasma.

However, only Mycoplasma genitalium is the causative agent of male urethritis.Pathogenicity provenis,Insurance coverage available from June 2022It became.

Therefore, insurance coverage may not apply unless the test is focused on Mycoplasma genitalium.

If you want to check for sexually transmitted diseases such as non-gonococcal and non-chlamydial mycoplasma urethritis and ureaplasma urethritis,Check whether medical treatment will be paid at your own expense at a clinic specializing in sexually transmitted diseasesLet's do it.

If you want to take the test anonymously

Because I don't want my family to know.If you want to be tested anonymously, you can pay for the treatment at your own expense.It will be.

If you receive medical treatment under insurance, the medical institution you visited will be listed on the medical expense notification that is sent to your home once a year, and your family may find out that you visited the hospital.

Therefore,Some people prefer to be tested anonymously without using their insurance card.It is.

If you don't want your family or friends to know about your STD test, you can do it anonymously.

If your partner is diagnosed with a sexually transmitted disease, insurance will cover the test.

If your partner is diagnosed with a sexually transmitted disease, there is a high possibility that you are infected as well., early testing and treatment is highly recommended, so STD testing is covered by insurance.

If your partner is diagnosed with a sexually transmitted disease and is examined, you may be asked to submit the following documents:

  • Partner test results
  • Partner's medical certificate

By clearly stating when and what kind of diagnosis your partner received, it will be easier for doctors to proceed with appropriate tests and treatment.

Both men and women can be affected by various diseases that can cause infertility or be life-threatening, so both men and women should undergo tests and receive appropriate treatment.

7 typical sexually transmitted diseases in Japan

The seven most common sexually transmitted diseases in Japan are:

Typical sexually transmitted diseases
  • chlamydia
  • gonorrhea
  • genital herpes
  • warts acuminata
  • syphilis
  • Candida
  • HIV

All tests are covered by insurance.Approximately 3,000 to 4,000 yen for the first visit (examination, examination, treatment)It is.

The re-examination will include additional medicines and tests, which will cost around 2,000 yen at most.

If you are paying for medical treatment yourself, please use the information as a reference only and ask the medical institution directly, as the costs vary greatly depending on the clinic.

1.Chlamydia

Ministry of Health, Labor and WelfareAnnual trends in the number of sexually transmitted disease reports by age groupAccording to , the number of chlamydia infections in 2022 will reach 30,136 people.The most common sexually transmitted disease in JapanYou can say that.

The incubation period for chlamydia is about 1 to 2 weeks.

Even if you have other sexually transmitted diseases, it is often associated with this disease, so you need to be careful.

2. Gonorrhea

Gonorrhea is highly contagious, and the Ministry of Health, Labor and WelfareAnnual trends in the number of sexually transmitted disease reports by age groupAccording to , the number of infected people in 2022 will be 9,993.The second most common sexually transmitted disease after chlamydiaIt is.

It is said that gonorrhea can be transmitted at a high rate of 30-50% during one sexual encounter.

If the infection is left untreated, it can cause infertility, so if you suspect it, go to the hospital as soon as possible.

3.Genital herpes

Herpesvirus is highly contagious,Sexually transmitted diseases that can be transmitted by sharing baths, toilets, and drinking glassesIt is.

When infected for the first time, symptoms tend to be more severe and recurrence is common.

There is no established treatment to completely eliminate the herpes virus, so it is important to take measures such as sleep deprivation and stress relief to suppress the symptoms.

4. Warts acuminata

Genital warts are a sexually transmitted disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.

If you are infected, symptoms may appear weeks or months later, but you may remain asymptomatic.

Treatment typically involves surgical excision or drug therapy (topical medications such as imiquimod).

5.Syphilis

Syphilis isSexually transmitted diseases whose number of patients has been increasing rapidly in recent yearsIt is.

Ministry of Health, Labor and WelfareAnnual trends in the number of sexually transmitted disease reports by age groupAccording to 2000, the number of people infected with syphilis was 759, but in 2022 there will be 13,221, an increase of approximately 17 times.

This is from the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare.Analysis of factors related to the increase in the number of syphilis patientsSo,The cause is the increase in tourists from overseas and non-store sex entertainment.It is said that

It is important to treat syphilis early with antibiotics.

Early detection and treatment are important, so if you have any suspicious symptoms, please visit a hospital or clinic.

6. Candida

Candida isSexually transmitted diseases common in womenHowever, it also occurs in men.

It is important to keep the genital area clean as self-infection is common due to resident bacteria.

7.HIV

HIV is the human immunodeficiency virus,AIDS (Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) may causeThere is.

AIDS is a scary disease in which the HIV virus infects lymphocytes, weakening the body's immune system and making it more susceptible to infections and cancer.

Originally, HIV was considered a "deadly disease" as there was no cure, but now new drugs have been developed and by continuing to take the drug, it is possible to reduce the amount of the virus and prevent the onset of AIDS.

However, HIV does not completely disappear from the body, and the virus grows again when you stop taking the drug, so you must continue taking the drug for the rest of your life.

Will STD test results be available on the same day?

For STD testing,"Same-day simple test" that gives results on the same dayThere is.

The same-day simple test is called the "immunochromatography method," and the test method is to make an extract from urine and drop it into a special test kit to determine the presence or absence of infection.

Immunochromatography methodThe advantage is that it is easy to use and results can be determined in a short time.It's a point.

On the contraryDisadvantages: Accuracy is low, and because the test uses urine, it can only confirm genital infections.It's a point.

This method does not allow examination of the throat or anus, so even if infection is suspected in these areas, it cannot be tested.

If you are clearly showing genital symptoms such as urethritis, you can proceed to treatment smoothly, but if you are not, please have a thorough examination at a medical institution.

If you are worried about a sexually transmitted disease, consider getting tested before it becomes serious.

In this article, we explained the conditions under which STD testing can be covered by insurance, as well as the cases in which medical treatment is self-pay and its costs.

There are three cases in which STD testing will be paid for at your own expense:

Cases in which STD tests are self-pay medical treatment
  • No symptoms
  • Suffering from a sexually transmitted disease that is difficult to get covered by insurance
  • If you want to take the test anonymously

You can be infected with sexually transmitted diseases even if you have no symptoms.

As the disease progresses, it can become life-threatening, so early detection and treatment are important.

Tests and treatments include self-pay medical treatment and medical treatment covered by insurance.Self-pay medical treatment costs more, but the test can be done anonymously, so you can receive treatment without anyone knowing.

Insurance medical treatmentThere is an advantage of having less out-of-pocket costs, but there is a risk that your family will find out.So, before the test, decide whether it will be a problem even if you find out.

To protect you and your precious partner, please consider getting tested if you feel even the slightest discomfort.
